topStories.headline: Gary McCoy Wins District 8 Supervisor Race in a Decisive First-Round Victory
topStories.dek: The former Pelosi aide took more than half of first-choice votes on November 3, ending a race that was upended when front-runner Manny Yekutiel dropped out last month.
topStories.body:
Gary McCoy declared victory Tuesday night in the race to become the next supervisor for District 8, which covers the Castro, Noe Valley, Duboce Triangle, Glen Park, Diamond Heights, and neighboring areas. With about 75 percent of ballots counted as of Thursday, McCoy held roughly 50 percent of first-choice votes — enough to clear a majority in the initial round of ranked-choice tabulation — and expanded to 18,419 votes after redistribution, against 10,453 for second-place finisher Darshini Patel. The San Francisco Department of Elections will not certify final results until December 3.

McCoy, who served as an aide to Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi, rose to front-runner status only after Emanuel "Manny" Yekutiel — a cafe owner and civic leader who had dominated fundraising — suspended his campaign in October following a report in the San Francisco Standard. Patel, a former DoorDash corporate employee, ran to McCoy's left; both candidates describe themselves as progressive Democrats.

McCoy has been publicly open about a past that included addiction and petty crime, calling his recovery central to how he would approach homelessness and drug policy in office. His stated priorities include filling vacant commercial storefronts, building housing, and improving street conditions and public transit. In remarks to supporters on election night, he said the district had taken a chance on him and that his win was about relationships and unity.

Current Supervisor Rafael Mandelman, whom McCoy will succeed, is termed out of office and will leave in January. Speaker Emerita Pelosi and her family campaigned for McCoy in the Castro in the days before the election.

topStories.headline: Castro Theatre's November Is Its Busiest Month Yet Since February Reopening
topStories.dek: With shows nearly every night through the end of the month, the restored 1922 landmark is fully living out the concert-venue future its operator promised.
topStories.body:
Nine months after reopening following a $41 million renovation, the Castro Theatre is running at a pace that would have been unimaginable during its years as a single-screen arthouse cinema. The venue's November calendar lists more than fifteen ticketed events — concerts, film screenings, and specialty shows — filling nearly every weeknight through the end of the month.

Highlights over the coming three weeks include indie-folk artist SYML tonight (Friday, November 6), Rodrigo y Gabriela on November 15, Jorja Smith on November 16, Hamilton Leithauser and Rostam on November 18, and the Castro Farmers' Market season-closing Wednesday on November 18 just steps away on Noe Street. The renovated hall also has a November 11 show by Icelandic composer Ólafur Arnalds, with a second date added November 12 after demand grew.

Another Planet Entertainment, the Berkeley-based promoter that took over the theater in 2022 and oversaw its renovation, removed the original raked orchestra seating to allow standing-room concerts — a change that divided the community before reopening. The reconfigured space has since proved capable of hosting acoustic seated shows as well as high-energy concerts, suggesting the flexible layout is delivering on its stated purpose.

Tickets for most November shows are available through the theater's website and standard ticketing platforms. Attendees are encouraged to arrive early and explore nearby restaurants and businesses along Castro Street.

topStories.headline: Castro Farmers' Market to Hold Its Final Wednesday of 2026 on November 18
topStories.dek: The weekly market on Noe Street will pause for the season after one last gathering, capping a year that included new vendors, returning favorites, and steady neighborhood turnout.
topStories.body:
The Castro Farmers' Market will close out its 2026 season on Wednesday, November 18, the San Francisco Bay Times reported this week. The market runs weekly on Noe Street near Market Street and has been a fixture of the neighborhood's midweek rhythm since it reopened in April.

This season saw several new vendors join the market alongside returning staples. Sconewild made its debut, Roli Roti's rotisserie chicken continued to draw lines at Noe and Market, and longtime favorites including Fifth Crow Farm and Bernal Bakery returned for another year. Community leaders including representatives of the Castro Merchants Association appeared at the season's opening in April.

November 18 will be the last opportunity for neighbors to shop the market before it takes its annual winter break. The Bay Times noted that the market is expected to return in 2027. Shoppers looking to stock up for the season should plan to arrive during regular market hours on the 18th.

events.title: SYML — Solo in North America 2026

events.title: Ólafur Arnalds at Castro Theatre
events.description: Icelandic ambient composer and producer Ólafur Arnalds plays two nights at the Castro Theatre; a second show on November 12 was added after the initial date sold out quickly.

events.title: Rodrigo y Gabriela at Castro Theatre
events.description: Mexican acoustic guitar duo Rodrigo y Gabriela bring their high-energy instrumental style to the Castro Theatre for a Sunday-evening performance.

events.title: Castro Farmers' Market — Final Day of 2026 Season
events.location: Noe Street at Market Street, Castro
events.description: The Castro Farmers' Market closes out its 2026 season with one last Wednesday gathering on Noe Street, featuring produce vendors, Roli Roti, and returning favorites. The market will pause until spring 2027.

events.title: Noe Valley Night Market
events.description: A free monthly evening market at the Noe Valley Town Square with live music, local food and retail vendors, and family-friendly programming. Free admission.

moreNews.headline: Glen Park Rec Center Field Closed Through November 23 for Turf Restoration
moreNews.body: The small field behind the Glen Park Recreation Center has been temporarily closed since October 19 for turf restoration work, according to the Glen Park Association. The closure is scheduled to run through Monday, November 23. Neighbors with children or dogs who rely on the field should plan accordingly through the end of the month.

moreNews.headline: Pottery and Jewelry Studio Bisk Opens at Former Noe and Market Laundromat
moreNews.body: The former Noe and Market Laundromat space at 262 Noe Street has reopened this month as Bisk Studio, a pottery and jewelry studio, the Bay Area Reporter noted in its 2026 Castro business roundup. The opening is part of a broader wave of new tenants filling Castro-area vacancies, a trend the Castro Community Benefit District has tracked through its I'm Available storefront campaign.

moreNews.headline: Romantic Bookstore Love Potion Library Listed as 'Coming Soon' to 284 Noe Street
moreNews.body: A new business called the Love Potion Library, described as a romantic bookstore, is slated to open at 284 Noe Street, the former location of Jeffery's Natural Foods, according to the Bay Area Reporter. Applicants have filed for a beer and wine sales license at the address. No opening date has been announced publicly.
